26: /// This is a helper function to store a pre-processed version of the verifying key.
27: /// This is roughly homologous to [`ark_groth16::PreparedVerifyingKey`].
28: /// Note that contrary to Arkworks, we don't store a "prepared" version of the gamma_g2_neg_pc,
29: /// delta_g2_neg_pc fields, because we can't use them with blst's pairing engine.
30: #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
31: pub struct PreparedVerifyingKey {
32:     /// The element vk.gamma_abc_g1,
33:     /// aka the `[gamma^{-1} * (beta * a_i + alpha * b_i + c_i) * G]`, where i spans the public inputs
34:     pub vk_gamma_abc_g1: Vec<G1Affine>,
35:     /// The element `e(alpha * G, beta * H)` in `E::GT`.
36:     pub alpha_g1_beta_g2: blst_fp12,
37:     /// The element `- gamma * H` in `E::G2`, for use in pairings.
38:     pub gamma_g2_neg_pc: G2Affine,
39:     /// The element `- delta * H` in `E::G2`, for use in pairings.
40:     pub delta_g2_neg_pc: G2Affine,
41: }
42: 
43: impl PreparedVerifyingKey {
44:     /// Deserialize the prepared verifying key from the serialized fields of vk_gamma_abc_g1, alpha_g1_beta_g2, gamma_g2_neg_pc, delta_g2_neg_pc
45:     pub fn deserialize(
46:         vk_gamma_abc_g1_bytes: &[u8],
47:         alpha_g1_beta_g2_bytes: &[u8],
48:         gamma_g2_neg_pc_bytes: &[u8],
49:         delta_g2_neg_pc_bytes: &[u8],
50:     ) -> Result<Self, FastCryptoError> {
51:         let mut vk_gamma_abc_g1: Vec<G1Affine> = Vec::new();
52:         for g1_bytes in vk_gamma_abc_g1_bytes.chunks(G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE) {
53:             let g1 = G1Affine::deserialize(g1_bytes).map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;
54:             vk_gamma_abc_g1.push(g1);
55:         }
56:         let alpha_g1_beta_g2 = bls_fq12_to_blst_fp12(
57:             &Fq12::deserialize(alpha_g1_beta_g2_bytes)
58:                 .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?,
59:         );
60: 
61:         let gamma_g2_neg_pc = G2Affine::deserialize(gamma_g2_neg_pc_bytes)
62:             .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;
63: 
64:         let delta_g2_neg_pc = G2Affine::deserialize(delta_g2_neg_pc_bytes)
65:             .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;
66: 
67:         Ok(PreparedVerifyingKey {
68:             vk_gamma_abc_g1,
69:             alpha_g1_beta_g2,
70:             gamma_g2_neg_pc,
71:             delta_g2_neg_pc,
72:         })
73:     }
74: 
75:     /// Serialize the prepared verifying key to its vectors form.
76:     pub fn as_serialized(&self) -> Result<Vec<Vec<u8>>, FastCryptoError> {
77:         let mut res = Vec::new();
78:         let mut vk_gamma = Vec::new();
79:         for g1 in &self.vk_gamma_abc_g1 {
80:             let mut g1_bytes = Vec::new();
81:             g1.serialize(&mut g1_bytes)
82:                 .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;
83:             vk_gamma.append(&mut g1_bytes);

85:         res.push(vk_gamma);

89:             .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;

94:             .serialize(&mut gamma_bytes)
95:             .map_err(|_| FastCryptoError::InvalidInput)?;
96:         res.push(gamma_bytes);

107: /// Takes an input [`ark_groth16::VerifyingKey`] `vk` and returns a `PreparedVerifyingKey`. This is roughly homologous to
108: /// [`ark_groth16::PreparedVerifyingKey::process_vk`], but uses a blst representation of the elements.
109: ///
110: /// ## Example:
111: /// ```
112: /// use fastcrypto_zkp::{dummy_circuits::Fibonacci, verifier::process_vk_special};
113: /// use ark_bls12_381::{Bls12_381, Fr};
114: /// use ark_ff::One;
115: /// use ark_groth16::{
116: ///     generate_random_parameters
117: /// };
118: /// use ark_std::rand::thread_rng;
119: ///
120: /// let mut rng = thread_rng();
121: /// let params = {
122: ///     let c = Fibonacci::<Fr>::new(42, Fr::one(), Fr::one()); // 42 constraints, initial a = b = 1 (standard Fibonacci)
123: ///     generate_random_parameters::<Bls12_381, _, _>(c, &mut rng).unwrap()
124: /// };
125: ///
126: /// // Prepare the verification key (for proof verification). Ideally, we would like to do this only
127: /// // once per circuit.
128: /// let pvk = process_vk_special(&params.vk);
129: /// ```
130: pub fn process_vk_special(vk: &VerifyingKey<Bls12_381>) -> PreparedVerifyingKey {
131:     let g1_alpha = bls_g1_affine_to_blst_g1_affine(&vk.alpha_g1);
132:     let g2_beta = bls_g2_affine_to_blst_g2_affine(&vk.beta_g2);
133:     let blst_alpha_g1_beta_g2 = {
134:         let mut tmp = blst_fp12::default();
135:         unsafe { blst_miller_loop(&mut tmp, &g2_beta, &g1_alpha) };
136: 
137:         let mut out = blst_fp12::default();
138:         unsafe { blst_final_exp(&mut out, &tmp) };
139:         out
140:     };
141:     PreparedVerifyingKey {
142:         vk_gamma_abc_g1: vk.gamma_abc_g1.clone(),
143:         alpha_g1_beta_g2: blst_alpha_g1_beta_g2,
144:         gamma_g2_neg_pc: vk.gamma_g2.neg(),
145:         delta_g2_neg_pc: vk.delta_g2.neg(),
146:     }
147: }
148: 
149: /// This helper constant makes it easier to use compute the linear combination involved in the pairing inputs.
150: const G1_IDENTITY: blst_p1 = blst_p1 {
151:     x: blst_fp { l: [0; 6] },
152:     y: blst_fp { l: [0; 6] },
153:     z: blst_fp { l: [0; 6] },
154: };
155: 
156: /// Returns the log base 2 of b in O(lg(N)) time.
157: fn log_2_byte(b: u8) -> usize {
158:     let mut r = u8::from(b > 0xF) << 2;
159:     let mut b = b >> r;
160:     let shift = u8::from(b > 0x3) << 1;
161:     b >>= shift + 1;
162:     r |= shift | b;
163:     r.into()
164: }
165: 
166: /// Returns a single scalar multiplication of `pt` by `b`.
167: fn mul(pt: &blst_p1, b: &blst_fr) -> blst_p1 {
168:     let mut scalar: blst_scalar = blst_scalar::default();
169:     unsafe {
170:         blst_scalar_from_fr(&mut scalar, b);
171:     }
172: 
173:     // Count the number of bytes to be multiplied.
174:     let mut i = scalar.b.len();
175:     while i != 0 && scalar.b[i - 1] == 0 {
176:         i -= 1;
177:     }
178: 
179:     let mut result = blst_p1::default();
180:     if i == 0 {
181:         return G1_IDENTITY;
182:     } else if i == 1 && scalar.b[0] == 1 {
183:         return *pt;
184:     } else {
185:         // Count the number of bits to be multiplied.
186:         unsafe {
187:             blst_p1_mult(
188:                 &mut result,
189:                 pt,
190:                 &(scalar.b[0]),
191:                 8 * i - 7 + log_2_byte(scalar.b[i - 1]),
192:             );
193:         }
194:     }
195:     result
196: }
197: 
198: /// Facade for the blst_p1_add_or_double function.
199: fn add_or_dbl(a: &blst_p1, b: &blst_p1) -> blst_p1 {
200:     let mut ret = blst_p1::default();
201:     unsafe {
202:         blst_p1_add_or_double(&mut ret, a, b);
203:     }
204:     ret
205: }
206: 
207: /// Computes the [\sum p_i * b_i, p_i in p_affine, b_i in coeffs] in G1.
208: fn g1_linear_combination(
209:     out: &mut blst_p1,
210:     p_affine: &[blst_p1_affine],
211:     coeffs: &[blst_fr],
212:     len: usize,
213: ) {
214:     if len < 8 {
215:         // Direct approach
216:         let mut tmp;
217:         *out = G1_IDENTITY;
218:         for i in 0..len {
219:             let mut p = blst_p1::default();
220:             unsafe { blst_p1_from_affine(&mut p, &p_affine[i]) };
221: 
222:             tmp = mul(&p, &coeffs[i]);
223:             *out = add_or_dbl(out, &tmp);
224:         }
225:     } else {
226:         let mut scratch: Vec<u8>;
227:         unsafe {
228:             scratch = vec![0u8; blst_p1s_mult_pippenger_scratch_sizeof(len)];
229:         }
230: 
231:         let mut scalars = vec![blst_scalar::default(); len];
232: 
233:         for i in 0..len {
234:             let mut scalar: blst_scalar = blst_scalar::default();
235:             unsafe {
236:                 blst_scalar_from_fr(&mut scalar, &coeffs[i]);
237:             }
238:             scalars[i] = scalar
239:         }
240: 
241:         let scalars_arg: [*const blst_scalar; 2] = [scalars.as_ptr(), ptr::null()];
242:         let points_arg: [*const blst_p1_affine; 2] = [p_affine.as_ptr(), ptr::null()];
243:         unsafe {
244:             blst_p1s_mult_pippenger(
245:                 out,
246:                 points_arg.as_ptr(),
247:                 len,
248:                 scalars_arg.as_ptr() as *const *const u8,
249:                 256,
250:                 scratch.as_mut_ptr() as *mut limb_t,
251:             );
252:         }
253:     }
254: }
255: 
256: /// This represents the multiplicative unit scalar, see fr_one_test
257: pub(crate) const BLST_FR_ONE: blst_fr = blst_fr {
258:     l: [
259:         8589934590,
260:         6378425256633387010,
261:         11064306276430008309,
262:         1739710354780652911,
263:     ],
264: };
265: 
266: /// Returns the result of the multi-pairing involved in the verification equation. This will then be compared to the pre-computed term
267: /// pvk.alpha_g1_beta_g2 to check the validity of the proof.
268: ///
269: /// The textbook Groth16 equation is (in additive notation):
270: /// e(A, B) = e(g * alpha, h * beta) + e(g * f, h * gamma) + e(C, h * delta)
271: /// where f is the linear combination of the a_i points in the verifying key with the input scalars
272: ///
273: /// Due to the pre-processing of e(g * alpha, h * beta), and using the pairing inverse, we instead compute:
274: /// e(A, B) + e(g * f, h * - gamma) + e(C, h * - delta).
275: ///
276: /// Eventually, we will compare this value to  e(g * alpha, h * beta)
277: ///
278: fn multipairing_with_processed_vk(
279:     pvk: &PreparedVerifyingKey,
280:     x: &[BlsFr],
281:     proof: &Proof<Bls12_381>,
282: ) -> blst_fp12 {
283:     // Linear combination: note that the arkworks interface assumes the 1st scalar is an implicit 1
284:     let pts: Vec<blst_p1_affine> = pvk
285:         .vk_gamma_abc_g1
286:         .iter()
287:         .map(bls_g1_affine_to_blst_g1_affine)
288:         .collect();
289:     let one = BLST_FR_ONE;
290:     let ss: Vec<blst_fr> = iter::once(one)
291:         .chain(x.iter().map(bls_fr_to_blst_fr))
292:         .collect();
293:     let mut out = blst_p1::default();
294:     g1_linear_combination(&mut out, &pts, &ss[..], ss.len());
295: 
296:     let blst_proof_a = bls_g1_affine_to_blst_g1_affine(&proof.a);
297:     let blst_proof_b = bls_g2_affine_to_blst_g2_affine(&proof.b);
298: 
299:     let mut blst_proof_1_g1 = blst_p1_affine::default();
300:     unsafe { blst_p1_to_affine(&mut blst_proof_1_g1, &out) };
301:     let blst_proof_1_g2 = bls_g2_affine_to_blst_g2_affine(&pvk.gamma_g2_neg_pc);
302: 
303:     let blst_proof_2_g1 = bls_g1_affine_to_blst_g1_affine(&proof.c);
304:     let blst_proof_2_g2 = bls_g2_affine_to_blst_g2_affine(&pvk.delta_g2_neg_pc);
305: 
306:     let dst = [0u8; 3];
307:     let mut pairing_blst = Pairing::new(false, &dst);
308:     pairing_blst.raw_aggregate(&blst_proof_b, &blst_proof_a);
309:     pairing_blst.raw_aggregate(&blst_proof_1_g2, &blst_proof_1_g1);
310:     pairing_blst.raw_aggregate(&blst_proof_2_g2, &blst_proof_2_g1);
311:     pairing_blst.as_fp12().final_exp()
312: }
313: 
314: /// Returns the validity of the Groth16 proof passed as argument. The format of the inputs is assumed to be in arkworks format.
315: /// See [`multipairing_with_processed_vk`] for the actual pairing computation details.
316: ///
317: /// ## Example
318: /// ```
319: /// use fastcrypto_zkp::{dummy_circuits::Fibonacci, verifier::{ process_vk_special, verify_with_processed_vk }};
320: /// use ark_bls12_381::{Bls12_381, Fr};
321: /// use ark_ff::One;
322: /// use ark_groth16::{
323: ///     create_random_proof, generate_random_parameters
324: /// };
325: /// use ark_std::rand::thread_rng;
326: ///
327: /// let mut rng = thread_rng();
328: ///
329: /// let params = {
330: ///     let circuit = Fibonacci::<Fr>::new(42, Fr::one(), Fr::one()); // 42 constraints, initial a = b = 1
331: ///     generate_random_parameters::<Bls12_381, _, _>(circuit, &mut rng).unwrap()
332: /// };
333: ///
334: /// // Prepare the verification key (for proof verification). Ideally, we would like to do this only
335: /// // once per circuit.
336: /// let pvk = process_vk_special(&params.vk);
337: ///
338: /// let proof = {
339: ///     let circuit = Fibonacci::<Fr>::new(42, Fr::one(), Fr::one()); // 42 constraints, initial a = b = 1
340: ///     // Create a proof with our parameters, picking a random witness assignment
341: ///     create_random_proof(circuit, &params, &mut rng).unwrap()
342: /// };
343: ///
344: /// // We provide the public inputs which we know are used in our circuits
345: /// // this must be the same as the inputs used in the proof right above.
346: /// let inputs: Vec<_> = [Fr::one(); 2].to_vec();
347: ///
348: /// // Verify the proof
349: /// let r = verify_with_processed_vk(&pvk, &inputs, &proof).unwrap();
350: /// ```
351: // TODO: due to arkworks incompatibilities in BLS12-381 point (de) serialization, we should probably implement a custom (de)serialization
352: // for those formats, see https://github.com/arkworks-rs/algebra/issues/257
353: pub fn verify_with_processed_vk(
354:     pvk: &PreparedVerifyingKey,
355:     x: &[BlsFr],
356:     proof: &Proof<Bls12_381>,
357: ) -> Result<bool, SynthesisError> {
358:     // Note the "+1" : this API implies the first scalar coefficient is 1 and not sent
359:     if (x.len() + 1) != pvk.vk_gamma_abc_g1.len() {
360:         return Err(SynthesisError::MalformedVerifyingKey);
361:     }
362: 
363:     let res = multipairing_with_processed_vk(pvk, x, proof);
364:     Ok(res == pvk.alpha_g1_beta_g2)
365: }

36: // Scalar Field conversions
37: /// Convert an Arkworks BLS12-381 scalar field element to a blst scalar field element.
38: pub fn bls_fr_to_blst_fr(fe: &BlsFr) -> blst_fr {
39:     debug_assert_eq!(fe.serialized_size(), SCALAR_SIZE);
40:     let mut bytes = [0u8; SCALAR_SIZE];
41:     fe.serialize_with_flags(&mut bytes[..], EmptyFlags).unwrap();
42: 
43:     let mut out = blst_fr::default();
44:     let bytes_u64 = u64s_from_bytes(&bytes);
45: 
46:     unsafe { blst_fr_from_uint64(&mut out, bytes_u64.as_ptr()) };
47:     out
48: }
49: 
50: /// Convert a blst scalar field element to an Arkworks BLS12-381 scalar field element.
51: pub fn blst_fr_to_bls_fr(fe: &blst_fr) -> BlsFr {
52:     let mut out = [0u64; 4];
53:     unsafe { blst_uint64_from_fr(out.as_mut_ptr(), fe) };
54:     let bytes = out.as_byte_slice();
55: 
56:     BlsFr::from_le_bytes_mod_order(bytes)
57: }

59: // Base Field conversions
60: /// Convert an Arkworks BLS12-381 prime field element to a blst prime field element.
61: pub fn bls_fq_to_blst_fp(f: &Fq) -> blst_fp {
62:     let mut fp_bytes_le = [0u8; G1_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE / 2];
63:     f.serialize_uncompressed(&mut fp_bytes_le[..])
64:         .expect("fp size correct");
65: 
66:     let mut blst_fp = blst_fp::default();
67:     unsafe {
68:         blst_fp_from_lendian(&mut blst_fp, fp_bytes_le.as_ptr());
69:     }
70:     blst_fp
71: }

73: /// Convert a blst prime field element to an Arkworks BLS12-381 prime field element.
74: pub fn blst_fp_to_bls_fq(f: &blst_fp) -> Fq {
75:     let mut out = [0u64; 6];
76:     unsafe { blst_uint64_from_fp(out.as_mut_ptr(), f) };
77:     let bytes = out.as_byte_slice();

83: /// Convert an Arkworks BLS12-381 quadratic extension field element to a blst quadratic extension
84: /// field element.
85: pub fn bls_fq2_to_blst_fp2(f: &Fq2) -> blst_fp2 {
86:     let mut fp_bytes_le = [0u8; G2_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE / 2];
87:     f.serialize_uncompressed(&mut fp_bytes_le[..])
88:         .expect("fp size correct");
89: 
90:     blst_fp2 {
91:         fp: fp_bytes_le
92:             .chunks(48)
93:             .map(|fp_bytes| {
94:                 let mut blst_fp = blst_fp::default();
95:                 unsafe {
96:                     blst_fp_from_lendian(&mut blst_fp, fp_bytes.as_ptr());
97:                 }
98:                 blst_fp
99:             })
100:             .collect::<Vec<blst_fp>>()
101:             .try_into()
102:             .unwrap(),
103:     }
104: }

106: /// Convert a blst quadratic extension field element to an Arkworks BLS12-381 quadratic extension
107: /// field element.
108: pub fn blst_fp2_to_bls_fq2(f: &blst_fp2) -> Fq2 {
109:     let [fp1, fp2] = f.fp;
110:     let bls_fp1 = blst_fp_to_bls_fq(&fp1);
111:     let bls_fp2 = blst_fp_to_bls_fq(&fp2);
112:     Fq2::new(bls_fp1, bls_fp2)
113: }

117: /// Convert an Arkworks BLS12-381 degree-6 extension field element to a blst degree-6 extension
118: /// field element.

122:     let c2 = bls_fq2_to_blst_fp2(&f.c2);

163: /// Convert an Arkworks BLS12-381 affine G1 point to a blst affine G1 point.
164: pub fn bls_g1_affine_to_blst_g1_affine(pt: &BlsG1Affine) -> blst_p1_affine {
165:     debug_assert_eq!(pt.uncompressed_size(), G1_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE);
166:     // BLST disagrees with Arkworks on the uncompressed representation of the infinity point on G1
167:     // https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/6382d67c72119d563975892ed49ba32e92d3d0da/src/e1.c#L153-L162
168:     // the infinity bit notwithstanding,
169:     // Arkworks: x = Fq::zero(), y = Fq::one()
170:     // BLST: x = y = Fq::zero()
171:     // BLST follows the standard here (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-pairing-friendly-curves-10#appendix-C)
172:     if pt.infinity {
173:         return blst_g1_affine_infinity();
174:     }
175:     let tmp_p1 = blst_p1_affine {
176:         x: bls_fq_to_blst_fp(&pt.x),
177:         y: bls_fq_to_blst_fp(&pt.y),
178:     };
179:     // See https://github.com/arkworks-rs/curves/issues/14 for why the double serialize
180:     // we're in fact applying correct masks that arkworks does not use. This may be solved
181:     // alternatively using https://github.com/arkworks-rs/algebra/issues/308 in a later release of
182:     // Arkworks.
183:     // Note: this is an uncompressed serialization - deserialization.
184:     let mut tmp2 = [0u8; 96];
185:     unsafe {
186:         blst_p1_affine_serialize(tmp2.as_mut_ptr(), &tmp_p1);
187:     };
188: 
189:     let mut g1 = blst_p1_affine::default();
190:     debug_assert_eq!(
191:         unsafe { blst_p1_deserialize(&mut g1, tmp2.as_ptr()) },
192:         BLST_ERROR::BLST_SUCCESS
193:     );
194:     g1
195: }

197: /// Convert a blst affine G1 point to an Arkworks BLS12-381 affine G1 point.
198: pub fn blst_g1_affine_to_bls_g1_affine(pt: &blst_p1_affine) -> BlsG1Affine {
199:     let mut out = [0u8; G1_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE];
200:     unsafe {
201:         blst_p1_affine_serialize(out.as_mut_ptr(), pt);
202:     }
203:     let infinity = out[0] == 0x40;
204:     // BLST disagrees with Arkworks on the uncompressed representation of the infinity point on G1
205:     // https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/6382d67c72119d563975892ed49ba32e92d3d0da/src/e1.c#L153-L162
206:     // the infinity bit notwithstanding,
207:     // Arkworks: x = Fq::zero(), y = Fq::one()
208:     // BLST: x = y = Fq::zero()
209:     // BLST follows the standard here (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-pairing-friendly-curves-10#appendix-C)
210:     if infinity {
211:         return bls_g1_affine_infinity();
212:     }
213:     let y = Fp384::from_be_bytes_mod_order(&out[48..]);
214:     let x = {
215:         // Mask away the flag bits (which Arkworks doesn't use).
216:         out[0] &= 0b0001_1111;
217:         Fp384::from_be_bytes_mod_order(&out[..48])
218:     };
219:     BlsG1Affine::new(x, y, infinity)
220: }

236:     // BLST disagrees with Arkworks on the uncompressed representation of the infinity point on G2
237:     // https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/6382d67c72119d563975892ed49ba32e92d3d0da/src/e2.c#L194-L203
238:     // the infinity bit notwithstanding,
239:     // Arkworks: x = Fq2::zero(), y = Fq2::one()
240:     // BLST: x = y = Fq2::zero()
241:     // BLST follows the standard here (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-pairing-friendly-curves-10#appendix-C)
242:     if pt.infinity {
243:         return blst_g2_affine_infinity();
244:     }
245:     let tmp_p2 = blst_p2_affine {
246:         x: bls_fq2_to_blst_fp2(&pt.x),
247:         y: bls_fq2_to_blst_fp2(&pt.y),
248:     };
249:     // See https://github.com/arkworks-rs/curves/issues/14 for why the double serialize
250:     // we're in fact applying correct masks that arkworks does not use. This may be solved
251:     // alternatively using https://github.com/arkworks-rs/algebra/issues/308 in a later release of
252:     // Arkworks.
253:     // Note: this is an uncompressed serialization - deserialization.
254:     let mut tmp2 = [0u8; G2_UNCOMPRESSED_SIZE];
255:     unsafe {
256:         blst_p2_affine_serialize(tmp2.as_mut_ptr(), &tmp_p2);
257:     };
258: 
259:     let mut g2 = blst_p2_affine::default();
260:     debug_assert_eq!(
261:         unsafe { blst_p2_deserialize(&mut g2, tmp2.as_ptr()) },
262:         BLST_ERROR::BLST_SUCCESS
263:     );
264:     g2
265: }

267: /// Convert a blst affine G2 point to an Arkworks BLS12-381 affine G2 point.
268: pub fn blst_g2_affine_to_bls_g2_affine(pt: &blst_p2_affine) -> BlsG2Affine {
269:     let ptx = blst_fp2_to_bls_fq2(&pt.x);
270:     let pty = blst_fp2_to_bls_fq2(&pt.y);
271: 
272:     let infinity = ptx == Fq2::zero();
273:     // BLST disagrees with Arkworks on the uncompressed representation of the infinity point on G2
274:     // https://github.com/supranational/blst/blob/6382d67c72119d563975892ed49ba32e92d3d0da/src/e2.c#L194-L203
275:     // the infinity bit notwithstanding,
276:     // Arkworks: x = Fq2::zero(), y = Fq2::one()
277:     // BLST: x = y = Fq2::zero()
278:     // BLST follows the standard here (see https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-irtf-cfrg-pairing-friendly-curves-10#appendix-C)
279:     if infinity {
280:         bls_g2_affine_infinity()
281:     } else {
282:         BlsG2Affine::new(ptx, pty, infinity)
283:     }
284: }

286: /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
287: // Zcash point encodings to Arkworks points and back       //
288: /////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////
289: 
290: // The standard for serialization of compressed G1, G2 points of BLS12-381
291: // is not followed by Arkworks 0.3.0. This is a translation layer to allow
292: // us to use (and receive) the standard serialization format.
293: // See section 5.4.9.2 of https://zips.z.cash/protocol/protocol.pdf
294: // and https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/draft-irtf-cfrg-bls-signature/ Appendix A
295: // for its choice as a standard.
296: 
297: // A note on BLST: blst uses Zcash point encoding formats across the board.
298: 
299: fn bls_fq_to_zcash_bytes(field: &Fq) -> [u8; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE] {
300:     let mut result = [0u8; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE];
301: 
302:     let rep = field.into_repr();
303: 
304:     result[0..8].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[5].to_be_bytes());
305:     result[8..16].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[4].to_be_bytes());
306:     result[16..24].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[3].to_be_bytes());
307:     result[24..32].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[2].to_be_bytes());
308:     result[32..40].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[1].to_be_bytes());
309:     result[40..48].copy_from_slice(&rep.0[0].to_be_bytes());
310: 
311:     result
312: }
313: 
314: fn bls_fq_from_zcash_bytes(bytes: &[u8; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE]) -> Option<Fq> {
315:     let mut tmp = BigInteger384::default();
316: 
317:     tmp.0[5] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[0..8].try_into().unwrap());
318:     tmp.0[4] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[8..16].try_into().unwrap());
319:     tmp.0[3] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[16..24].try_into().unwrap());
320:     tmp.0[2] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[24..32].try_into().unwrap());
321:     tmp.0[1] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[32..40].try_into().unwrap());
322:     tmp.0[0] = u64::from_be_bytes(bytes[40..48].try_into().unwrap());
323: 
324:     Fq::from_repr(tmp)
325: }
326: 
327: struct EncodingFlags {
328:     is_compressed: bool,
329:     is_infinity: bool,
330:     is_lexicographically_largest: bool,
331: }
332: 
333: impl From<&[u8]> for EncodingFlags {
334:     fn from(bytes: &[u8]) -> Self {
335:         Self {
336:             is_compressed: ((bytes[0] >> 7) & 1) == 1,
337:             is_infinity: (bytes[0] >> 6) & 1 == 1,
338:             is_lexicographically_largest: (bytes[0] >> 5) & 1 == 1,
339:         }
340:     }
341: }
342: 
343: impl EncodingFlags {
344:     fn encode_flags(&self, bytes: &mut [u8]) {
345:         if self.is_compressed {
346:             bytes[0] |= 1 << 7;
347:         }
348: 
349:         if self.is_infinity {
350:             bytes[0] |= 1 << 6;
351:         }
352: 
353:         if self.is_compressed && !self.is_infinity && self.is_lexicographically_largest {
354:             bytes[0] |= 1 << 5;
355:         }
356:     }
357: }
358: 
359: /// This deserializes an Arkworks G1Affine point from a Zcash point encoding.
360: pub fn bls_g1_affine_from_zcash_bytes(bytes: &[u8; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE]) -> Option<BlsG1Affine> {
361:     // Obtain the three flags from the start of the byte sequence.
362:     let flags = EncodingFlags::from(&bytes[..]);
363: 
364:     if !flags.is_compressed {
365:         return None; // We only support compressed points.
366:     }
367: 
368:     if flags.is_infinity {
369:         return Some(BlsG1Affine::default());
370:     }
371:     // Attempt to obtain the x-coordinate.
372:     let x = obtain_x_coordinate(bytes.as_slice())?;
373: 
374:     BlsG1Affine::get_point_from_x(x, flags.is_lexicographically_largest)
375: }
376: 
377: /// This serializes an Arkworks G1Affine point into a Zcash point encoding.
378: pub fn bls_g1_affine_to_zcash_bytes(p: &BlsG1Affine) -> [u8; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE] {
379:     let mut result = bls_fq_to_zcash_bytes(&p.x);
380:     let encoding = EncodingFlags {
381:         is_compressed: true,
382:         is_infinity: p.infinity,
383:         is_lexicographically_largest: p.y > -p.y,
384:     };
385:     encoding.encode_flags(&mut result[..]);
386:     result
387: }
388: 
389: /// This deserializes an Arkworks G2Affine point from a Zcash point encoding.
390: pub fn bls_g2_affine_from_zcash_bytes(bytes: &[u8; G2_COMPRESSED_SIZE]) -> Option<BlsG2Affine> {
391:     // Obtain the three flags from the start of the byte sequence
392:     let flags = EncodingFlags::from(&bytes[..]);
393: 
394:     if !flags.is_compressed {
395:         return None; // We only support compressed points.
396:     }
397: 
398:     if flags.is_infinity {
399:         return Some(BlsG2Affine::default());
400:     }
401: 
402:     let xc1 = obtain_x_coordinate(bytes.as_slice())?;
403:     let xc0 = {
404:         let mut tmp = [0; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE];
405:         tmp.copy_from_slice(&bytes[48..96]);
406: 
407:         bls_fq_from_zcash_bytes(&tmp)?
408:     };
409: 
410:     let x = Fq2::new(xc0, xc1);
411: 
412:     BlsG2Affine::get_point_from_x(x, flags.is_lexicographically_largest)
413: }
414: 
415: /// This serializes an Arkworks G2Affine point into a Zcash point encoding.
416: pub fn bls_g2_affine_to_zcash_bytes(p: &BlsG2Affine) -> [u8; G2_COMPRESSED_SIZE] {
417:     let mut bytes = [0u8; G2_COMPRESSED_SIZE];
418: 
419:     let c1_bytes = bls_fq_to_zcash_bytes(&p.x.c1);
420:     let c0_bytes = bls_fq_to_zcash_bytes(&p.x.c0);
421:     bytes[0..48].copy_from_slice(&c1_bytes[..]);
422:     bytes[48..96].copy_from_slice(&c0_bytes[..]);
423: 
424:     let encoding = EncodingFlags {
425:         is_compressed: true,
426:         is_infinity: p.infinity,
427:         is_lexicographically_largest: p.y > -p.y,
428:     };
429: 
430:     encoding.encode_flags(&mut bytes[..]);
431:     bytes
432: }
433: 
434: // Attempt to obtain x_coordinate
435: fn obtain_x_coordinate(bytes: &[u8]) -> Option<Fq> {
436:     let mut tmp = [0; G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE];
437:     // this is safe as the private obtain_x_coordinate function is only invoked with G1 (48) and
438:     // G2 (96) size inputs.
439:     tmp.copy_from_slice(&bytes[0..G1_COMPRESSED_SIZE]);
440: 
441:     // Mask away the flag bits
442:     tmp[0] &= 0b0001_1111;
443: 
444:     bls_fq_from_zcash_bytes(&tmp)
445: }

20: struct Blake2sCircuit {
21:     input: [u8; 32],
22:     blake2_seed: [u8; 32],
23:     pub expected_output: [u8; 32],
24: }
25: 
26: impl Blake2sCircuit {
27:     fn new() -> Self {
28:         // We're going to prove knowledge of the blake2 hash of this secret
29:         // see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cluedo
30:         let statement = b"butler in the yard with a wrench";
31:         let bytes = statement.to_vec();
32: 
33:         // as a sanity-check, we'll also compute the blake2 hash of the secret
34:         // with the reference implementation
35: 
36:         // Blake2s takes a seed parameter. We use a default seed.
37:         let seed: [u8; 32] = [0u8; 32];
38: 
39:         // Compute the hash by traditional means.
40:         let mut h = Blake2s256::new_with_prefix(seed);
41:         h.update(&bytes);
42:         let hash_result = h.finalize();
43: 
44:         // We use the arkworks API for blake2s as well and check it matches
45:         let input: [u8; 32] = bytes[..].try_into().unwrap();
46:         let out = B2SPRF::evaluate(&seed, &input).unwrap();
47: 
48:         // the traditional means and the arkworks implementation match
49:         assert_eq!(hash_result.as_slice(), out.as_slice());
50: 
51:         // at this stage, we can publish the seed and the expected hash output,
52:         // and we'll prove we know the input
53:         Self {
54:             input: statement.to_owned(),
55:             blake2_seed: seed,
56:             expected_output: out,
57:         }
58:     }
59: }
60: 
61: impl ConstraintSynthesizer<Fr> for Blake2sCircuit {
62:     fn generate_constraints(self, cs: ConstraintSystemRef<Fr>) -> Result<(), SynthesisError> {
63:         // initialize the blake2s gadget and allocate the seed
64:         let seed_var = UInt8::new_input_vec(cs.clone(), &self.blake2_seed).unwrap();
65: 
66:         // declare the witnesses
67:         let input_var = UInt8::new_witness_vec(cs.clone(), &self.input).unwrap();
68: 
69:         // declare the public intended output
70:         let desired_out_var = <Blake2sGadget as PRFGadget<_, Fr>>::OutputVar::new_input(cs, || {
71:             Ok(self.expected_output)
72:         })
73:         .unwrap();
74: 
75:         // link the intended output to a blake2s computation on the input, i.e. constrain Blake2s(seed, input) == output
76:         let output_var = Blake2sGadget::evaluate(&seed_var, &input_var).unwrap();
77:         output_var.enforce_equal(&desired_out_var).unwrap();
78: 
79:         Ok(())
80:     }
81: }

90:
